newsitem.title: ECUADOR: SOCCER-ECUADOR SHOCK EIGHT-MAN URUGUAY WITH 4-0 WIN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ECUADOR SHOCK EIGHT-MAN URUGUAY WITH 4-0 WIN.

text.p: Unrated Ecuador pulled off a stunning World Cup upset on Wednesday as they hammered Uruguay, one of the game's traditional powers, 4-0 in a South American qualifier.

In addition to seeing their chances of reaching the finals severely dented, Uruguay could find themselves in trouble with FIFA after having three players sent off, two for dissent and one for violence.
Uruguay had already been warned by soccer's governing body about their behaviour after receiving seven yellow cards during a 1-0 defeat away to Chile last year.
Ecuador, meanwhile, resurrected their chances of playing in the World Cup finals for the first time.

Under coach Francisco Maturana, who took his native Colombia to the 1990 and 1994 World Cup finals, Ecuador had already beaten Argentina but their challenge appeared to be faltering after they lost their last three qualifying games.
Midfielder Alex Aguinaga settled the home team's nerves, however, when he shot them in front after six minutes.

Ecuador, with the advantage of playing at 2,800 metres above sea level, controlled the game and extended their lead in the 69th minute when Agustin Delgado pounced on a mistake by goalkeeper Roberto Siboldi.
Until that point, Siboldi had kept Uruguay alive with a series of important saves.
Four minutes later, Uruguay defender Gustavo Mendez was sent off for a violent tackle and in the 77th minute Delgado scored again, this time with an individual effort.
Substitute Kleber Chala wrapped up the scoring two minutes from the end, prompting the Uruguayans to lose their self control completely.

Star striker Daniel Fonseca was dismissed for arguing with hardline Argentine referee Javier Castrilli immediately after Chala's goal and team mate Nelson Abeijon followed in injury time for the same offence.
Castrilli is known as "lawman" in his own country, where he has upset numerous people.
The result allowed Ecuador to leap-frog Uruguay in the single South American group, which reached the halfway stage on Wednesday. Ecuador have 12 points from eight games, and Uruguay 10.

Ecuador: 12-Giovanni Ibarra, 3-Wagner Rivera, 14-Alberto Montano, 2-Ivan Hurtado, 6-Luis Capurro, 4-Simon Ruiz, 8-Jimmy Blandon, 15-Oswaldo De la Cruz (Klever Chala 81st min), 7-Gilson De Souza (Angel Fernandez, 81st), 10-Alex Aguinaga, 13-Agustin Delgado.

Uruguay: 1-Roberto Siboldi, 2-Washington Tais, 3-Paolo Montero, 4-Jose Herrera, 6-Gustavo Mendez, 5-Eber Moas, 8-Nelson Abeijon, 17-Fabin O'Neill, 18-Gabriel Cedres (Dario Silva, 54), 10-Enzo Francescoli (Marcelo Saralegui, 64th), 13-Sebastian Abreu (Daniel Fonseca, 54th).
